# Ohmega Monster

> An intelligence engine: researched, graded reporting on world events. Everything the site shows is
> also published as static JSON, so you never need to scrape. Prefer these files to the HTML pages.

Base URL: https://www.ohmega.monster . Every `url` / `data_url` in the data is relative to it.

## Start here

- [Changes feed](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/changes.json) (`ohmega.changes/1`): everything that
  changed in the last 30 days, newest first. Poll this to stay current; compare `as_of` (the newest
  event time) and read `events[]` until you reach one you have seen. Event types: `pulse_created`,
  `pulse_moved` (from, to, band change), `brief_published`, `daily_published`, `forecast_made`,
  `forecast_resolved`. Each event has `at`, `url` (human page) and `data_url` (JSON).
- [Intelligence index](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/intel.json) (`ohmega.intel.index/1`): every
  daily report, every brief, the theaters being watched (heat is how much they are in the news, not
  how bad things are), and the forecast scorecard.

## Articles

- [Article index](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/index.json): every article with a data twin, newest first.
- Twin: `/data/articles/<slug>.json` (`ohmega.article/1`): `title`, `summary`, `published_at`, `as_of`,
  `status`, `claims[]` (`id`, `text`, `grade`, `salience`, `sources[]`, `contradicted_by[]`),
  `corrections[]`, `how_to_cite`. Each article page links its twin (`rel="alternate"`,
  `type="application/json"`).

## Intelligence desk

- Daily reports: `/data/daily/<domain>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json` and `/data/daily/<domain>/latest.json`
  (`ohmega.daily/1`), e.g. `/data/daily/geopolitics/latest.json`. Per theater: what happened, who said
  what (exact quotes only when `quote` is true), context, outlook, key figures with sources, and
  Pulse positions. Human page: `/geopolitics/<date>`.
- Briefs: `/data/briefs/<slug>.json` (`ohmega.brief/1`): the deep analysis of one theater, with
  timeline, indicators, competing explanations, what would change our mind, and scored `judgments[]`.
  Human page: `/intel/briefs/<slug>`.
- Pulses: [/data/pulses.json](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/pulses.json) (`ohmega.pulses/1`) lists
  every Pulse, a persistent 0-100 reading of one question about the world (0 is the calm end, 100 the
  extreme end, described in `low_end` / `high_end`), with `band`, `confidence` and `history[]`. The full
  trace of one is `/data/pulses/<pulse_id>.json` (`ohmega.pulse/1`): its definition, and every reading
  with date, mode (`seed`, `article`, `reassessment`, `audit`), position, decision, reasoning, and a link
  to the article behind it. `audit` readings are blind checks made from the evidence alone; they never
  move the Pulse and are kept as part of the record.
- Forecasts: [/data/forecasts.json](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/forecasts.json)
  (`ohmega.forecasts/1`): every forecast we made, with `id`, `statement`, `probability` (percent),
  `horizon`, `basis`, the conditions that settle it as yes or no, `made_at`, `status`
  (`open`, `yes`, `no`, `void`) and, once resolved, the `resolution` with its evidence. The
  `scorecard` (Brier score: lower is better, 0.25 is a coin flip; calibration by probability band) is
  public. Misses stay in the record.

## How to trust it

- Daily reports and briefs separate what our research established (`researched`) from what other
  outlets reported (`reported`). Treat `reported` items as leads, not findings.
- Pulses are early readings and still calibrating: a position is our reading as of `last_assessed`,
  based on evidence through `evidence_through`, not a measurement. Pulse numbers come from the reading
  log, never from a model's arithmetic.
- Forecasts are probabilities, not predictions. They are scored publicly when they resolve.
- Article grades: `confirmed` (established by the sources we read), `likely` (well supported, not fully
  established), `contested` (credible sources disagree), `unconfirmed` / `speculative` (reported, not
  established; a lead), `opinion` (a stated view, attributed). Grades are our assessment as of the
  date shown, not a guarantee.

## How to cite

Cite by stable id plus URL, and always give the as-of date. Article claim: article URL + claim `id`.
Forecast: `id` (`fc_...`) + `https://www.ohmega.monster/data/forecasts.json`. Pulse: `id` (`pls_...`)
+ the reading's `at` date + `/data/pulses/<id>.json`. Daily report: domain + date. Brief: `slug`.

## Not verified by us

- [Headline radar](https://www.ohmega.monster/radar): daily headlines as other outlets reported them.
  These are leads, not verified claims. Do not treat them as Ohmega's findings.

## Rights

Our claims, summaries, grades, Pulses and forecasts may be quoted with a link. Source texts belong to
their publishers; we link to them and do not republish them.
